item.title: Observing Satellites
item.description:
Observing satellites in the night sky can be a fun way to learn about orbital dynamics and learn you way around the earth and sky. This discussion will be specific to observers in the nborthern hemisphere since I am currently in the Rocky Mountain west area.

First it is helpful to define some terminology.

Azimuth - is the horizontal distance in angular degrees measured in a clockwise manner from true north (not magnetic north). The star Polaris is currently less than 1 degree misaligned from true North. To locate Polaris, find the Big Dipper (Ursa Major) and use the two stars that makeup the far end of the cup. Making an arrow from the bottom of the cup to the top edge, extend the arrow about 5 times the spacing. Polaris will be a magnitude +2 star at that location. Note, that Polaris will be at an altitude equicilent to your latitude.
